 Mandaue intensifies dengue prevention after 2 deaths in November
 By Kaiser Jan Fuentes
 November 19, 2026
 30
 Resize 
 Small 
 Medium 
 Large 
 MANDAUE CITY — The city recorded two dengue-related deaths in November as cases continued to increase this year, prompting the City Health Office (CHO) to intensify surveillance and prevention efforts in the barangay level.
 City health officer Dr. Debra Maria Catulong identified the fatalities as residents of Barangay Tabok and Barangay Umapad, both of whom were brought to hospitals and reported as dengue-related deaths.
 “Naabot gyud to sila sa hospital. Reported gyud siya as dengue deaths,” Catulong said.
 (Both patients reached the hospital, and their cases were officially reported as dengue-related deaths.)
 Catulong also said dengue cases in Mandaue have increased this year compared to 2025, when the city recorded 520 cases and three deaths for the entire year.

 However, the CHO did not disclose the latest case count for 2026.
 Previous reports placed the city's tally at 373 cases and one death from Jan. 1 to July 30.
 Advertisement 
 Catulong said the CHO automatically dispatches its surveillance team whenever a dengue infection or fatality is reported through its monitoring system.
 Health personnel visit affected households and nearby areas to determine how long patients experienced symptoms, identify possible delays in seeking medical attention, inspect potential mosquito breeding sites and educate families and surrounding residents about prevention.
 The investigations cover all reported infections, not just fatal cases, to assess the risk of further transmission within communities.
 Catulong emphasized that eliminating mosquito breeding sites remains the most important measure against dengue.
 Advertisement 
 She urged residents to follow the Department of Health's 4S strategy: search and destroy mosquito breeding sites, seek early consultation, adopt self-protection measures and support targeted spraying or fogging in areas experiencing outbreaks.
 “Kung wala tay breeding sites sa mosquitoes, walay mabuhi nga mosquitoes. So, pangitaon tong potential breeding sites and then pangitaon tong wagtangon,” she said.
 (If there are no mosquito breeding sites, no mosquitoes will survive. Potential breeding sites must therefore be identified and eliminated.)
 Residents who develop a fever should consult a doctor within the first two days of symptoms to receive proper assessment and early intervention.
 Advertisement 
 The CHO outpatient department and Mandaue City Hospital have established dengue fast lanes to prioritize patients with fever or a recent history of fever.
 Suspected patients can avail themselves of free laboratory examinations, including complete blood count, platelet count and NS1 antigen tests. 
 The facilities also provide free paracetamol and hydration fluids.
 Catulong also encouraged residents to use Food and Drug Administration-approved mosquito repellents and wear loose-fitting, long-sleeved clothing to reduce exposure to mosquito bites.
 Advertisement 
 Fogging and misting operations are limited to identified dengue hotspots, particularly during outbreaks, as these procedures only kill adult mosquitoes temporarily and do not eliminate breeding sites.
 The CHO also conducts community lectures and entomological surveys to identify areas with mosquito breeding activity.
 All 27 barangay have activated their respective dengue brigades and prepared community prevention plans that include regular monitoring and cleanup drives.
 Catulong noted that dengue remains a year-round concern, although cases generally increase during the rainy season because stagnant water provides breeding grounds for mosquitoes. 
 Advertisement 
 Cases also occur during summer, making continuous prevention necessary.
 She called on neighboring cities and municipalities to coordinate their cleanup and prevention activities, stressing that mosquito control requires cooperation beyond individual local government boundaries.
